newsitem.title: CHINA: China welcomes France defence chief amid rosy ties.
newsitem.headline: China welcomes France defence chief amid rosy ties.

text.p: French Defence Minister Charles Millon on Monday met his Chinese counterpart in Beijing on a visit hailed by China as another major step forward in rapidly warming Sino-French relations.

"The current visit of the French defence minister will make a great contribution to the development of the relations between the two countries and the two armed forces," the Xinhua news agency quoted Chinese Defence Minister Chi Haotian as telling Millon.
Premier Li Peng also met Millon and praised Paris for its decision not to co-sponsor a U.N. resolution critical of Beijing's human rights record, state television said.
"On the human rights question, different nations...should use equal dialogue in place of unhappy confrontation," the television report quoted Li as saying.

France said last month it would not co-sponsor a motion to criticise China's human rights policies at the U.N. Human Rights Commission in Geneva, saying Beijing had made progress on protecting basic freedoms.
"With the restoration and development of bilateral ties in the past few years, the friendly cooperation between the two armed forces has entered a new phase," Chi was quoted as saying.

Denmark said at the weekend it would press ahead with the resolution to censure China, prompting a stern warning from Beijing that political and economic ties would be severely damaged by such a move.

Paris also won favour with Beijing in 1994 by agreeing to halt all new arms sales to Taiwan, the Nationalist-led island that has been the arch-rival of the communist mainland since the two were split at the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949.
Taipei said last month that a deal to buy shoulder-fired missiles from France had collapsed, but declined to say if pressure from Beijing was to blame.
Sino-French relations further warmed when Premier Li visited Paris last year and signed multi-billion dollar business contracts with French firms.
